descriptionChirho: Collective noun denoting domesticated animals — cattle, sheep, goats, donkeys — viewed as movable property; used in pastoral, sacrificial, plague, and enumeration contexts across all grammatical inflections and pronominal suffixes, consistently rendered as Arabic mashiya/mawashi, Korean gachuk, and Swahili mifugo.

Abstract or commercial sense retaining the root meaning of q-n-h (to acquire): the act of purchasing, the price of acquisition, or property/possessions viewed as what has been acquired; distinguished by Arabic shira (purchase), muqtana/qinya (acquired property) rather than mashiya (livestock), and by Korean soyu (possession) or maemaeham (buying-selling) rather than gachuk (livestock), and Swahili mali (wealth) or makundi (property groups) rather than mifugo (livestock).
